reasons: Claimed status is compliant and the rendered redline is byte-identical to the original with no counterparty comment, which is exactly what a compliant finding should look like — nothing is being over-flagged or wrongly rewritten.

The cited text supports the rationale: Section 3.6 (p0131) grants the Issuer, Depositor and other transaction parties (our side) an annual, reasonable-notice review of the Servicer's (Cellco's) records at Cellco's offices during business hours, and Section 3.9(e) (p0146) gives us access to Cellco's Receivable Files and receivables systems. Both rights run against the counterparty, not against us.

The AUDIT rule targets audit/inspection rights binding the Customer (frequency, notice, cost, system access). No provision in the cited material imposes audit obligations, audit costs or system access on the Issuer/Depositor, so the rule's risk is not engaged; treating this as compliant rather than a deviation or 'missing' clause is the correct classification for a protective rule.

Sub-elements noted only in the rationale (review confined to Servicer's offices, subject to Cellco's security/confidentiality/privacy policies) are correctly recorded as customary observations rather than escalated as deviations.

Deterministic check ('audit frequency limited') passes, consistent with the once-per-calendar-year limitation in the cited text, and there is no changed-character ratio concern since no edit was made.
